The Moon is the only natural satellite of Earth, orbiting the planet in an elliptical path with an average distance of approximately 378,000 kilometers (235,000 mi) [1]. Because of gravitational attraction and tidal forces, the Moon is tidally locked, meaning it always shows the same near side to Earth [1]. It completes a synodic orbit relative to the Earth and Sun every 29.5 days [1].

The term also refers to *The Moon Is Down*, a 1942 propaganda novel by John Steinbeck regarding military occupation [2], or Moon Moon Sen, an Indian actress and politician [3].

Sources:
- Moon: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon
- The Moon Is Down: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Moon_Is_Down
- Moon Moon Sen: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon_Moon_Sen

Instead of buttermilk
for 1 cup
- 1 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar, plus milk to make 1 cup; stand 5–10 minutes
then: Keep the baking soda the recipe calls for: the acid in the swap is what it reacts with
- ¾ cup plain yogurt + ¼ cup milk
then: Thicker than buttermilk, so add 1–2 tbsp milk if the batter looks stiff
- 1 cup kefir
The usual kitchen equivalents. Any swap changes the taste or texture a little; the first one listed is the closest.
